scenes.frame: The Vikings haven't lost yet. Can the Lions change that?
Both teams come in with winning records.
Two of the better teams in the league, head to head.
A big one at the top of the standings.
Two winning teams, and only one can leave happy.

voice.hook: 3 rushing touchdowns! Tony Pollard just had the biggest day of Week 7. We've got every score, the games everyone is talking about, our player of the week, the stat leaders and the matchups you can't miss in Week 8. Let's go!
voice.f0: Let's run through every final from Week 7. The Bears beat the Patriots, 30 to 24, behind 130 receiving yards from Luther Burden III. The Steelers took down the Saints, 16 to 10, behind 101 rushing yards from Jaylen Warren. The Falcons got past the 49ers, 29 to 20, behind 213 passing yards from Michael Penix Jr.. The Browns edged the Titans, 27 to 24, behind 96 rushing yards from Quinshon Judkins. The Vikings beat the Colts, 16 to 10. The Dolphins held off the Jets, 28 to 25, behind 208 passing yards from Malik Willis. The Buccaneers blew out the Panthers, 43 to 13, behind 106 rushing yards from Bucky Irving.
voice.f1: Here's the rest. The Bengals blew out the Ravens, 35 to 13, behind 292 passing yards from Joe Burrow. The Giants beat the Texans in overtime, 27 to 21, behind 124 rushing yards from Cam Skattebo. The Broncos took down the Cardinals, 30 to 16, behind 73 rushing yards from Bo Nix. The Lions squeaked past the Packers, 20 to 17, behind 91 receiving yards from Jameson Williams. The Rams beat the Raiders, 35 to 21, behind 68 receiving yards from Puka Nacua. The Seahawks took down the Chiefs, 20 to 3, behind 150 receiving yards from Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The Cowboys handled the Eagles, 38 to 21, behind 74 receiving yards from CeeDee Lamb.
voice.g0: Now, the games everyone is talking about. This one needed overtime! The Giants beat the Texans, 27 to 21. Cam Skattebo ran for 124 yards and a touchdown. Malik Nabers caught 7 passes for 111 yards. The Giants move to 4, 2 and 1, and the Texans fall to 2 and 5.
voice.g1: Upset alert! The Falcons took down the 49ers at home, 29 to 20. Christian McCaffrey caught 6 passes for 61 yards. Michael Penix Jr. threw for 213 yards and 3 touchdowns without an interception. The Falcons move to 3 and 4, and the 49ers fall to 6 and 1.
voice.g2: A nail-biter! The Browns held off the Titans, 27 to 24. Tony Pollard ran for 129 yards and 3 touchdowns. Quinshon Judkins ran for 96 yards and 2 touchdowns. The Browns move to 5 and 2, and the Titans fall to 1 and 6.
voice.g3: A nail-biter! The Dolphins held off the Jets, 28 to 25. Malik Willis threw for 208 yards and 2 touchdowns without an interception. Mason Taylor caught 5 passes for 62 yards and 2 touchdowns. The Dolphins move to 1 and 5, and the Jets fall to 2 and 5.
voice.g4: A nail-biter! The Lions held off the Packers, 20 to 17. Jameson Williams caught 5 passes for 91 yards and 2 touchdowns. Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 9 passes for 153 yards. The Lions move to 4 and 2, and the Packers fall to 4 and 3.
voice.g5: Upset alert! The Seahawks took down the Chiefs at home, 20 to 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown. Emanuel Wilson ran for 100 yards and a touchdown. The Seahawks move to 4 and 3, and the Chiefs fall to 5 and 1.
voice.num: Week 7 by the numbers. 632 points were scored across 14 games. Seven of them were one-score games, and one went to overtime. The longest play of the week was a 63 yard catch by Caleb Douglas. And the Buccaneers put up the most points, with 43.
voice.tm: The best offense of the week belonged to the Browns, with 491 total yards against the Titans. The toughest defense? The Seahawks, who allowed just 213 yards. The Falcons forced 4 turnovers. And the biggest win of the week was the Buccaneers, by 30 points over the Panthers.
voice.l0: On to the stat leaders. The top passer of the week was Drake Maye, with 321 yards. That's more than three football fields! Caleb Williams was next with 308, followed by Deshaun Watson with 308.
voice.l1: The top rusher of the week was Javonte Williams, with 155 yards. That's a field and a half! Tony Pollard was next with 129, followed by Cam Skattebo with 124.
voice.l2: The top receiver of the week was Amon-Ra St. Brown, with 153 yards. That's a field and a half! Jaxon Smith-Njigba was next with 150, followed by Tee Higgins with 148.
voice.def: On defense, Yaya Diaby led everyone with 3 sacks. D'Marco Jackson picked off a pass. And Alex Singleton was everywhere, with 19 tackles.
voice.pow: And now, our player of the week... Tony Pollard! He ran for 129 yards and 3 touchdowns. The Titans lost to the Browns, 27 to 24, and he scored 36.5 fantasy points. Honorable mentions go to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Joe Burrow.
voice.fan: In fantasy football, Tony Pollard led everyone with 36.5 points in PPR leagues. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 31.3, Joe Burrow had 28.9, and Zay Flowers and Drake Maye rounded out the top five.
voice.std: After Week 7, the Vikings have the best record in the league at 6 and 0. The 49ers, the Chiefs and the Bills are right behind them, with the Browns, Broncos, Steelers and Bears close behind.
voice.n0: Around the NBA this week, nobody was better than Luka Doncic. 52 points, 8 rebounds and 10 assists against the Jazz, on 17 of 30 shooting!
voice.n1: Nikola Jokic dropped 35 on the Pelicans, on 12 of 23 shooting, with 15 rebounds and 10 assists.
voice.n2: And Cooper Flagg had 29 points, 6 rebounds and 11 assists against the Heat, on 12 of 23 shooting.
voice.nbr: A few more big NBA games this week. Anthony Edwards scored 45 against the Heat. Alperen Sengun scored 29 against the Hawks. Jalen Johnson scored 26 against the Rockets.
voice.sl: Now let's look ahead to Week 8. Fourteen games are on the schedule, starting Thursday night with the Panthers at the Packers.
voice.m0: Here are the matchups you can't miss. Sunday at 1, the Vikings, at 6 and 0, visit the Lions, at 4 and 2. The Vikings haven't lost yet. Can the Lions change that?
voice.m1: Sunday afternoon, the Chiefs, at 5 and 1, visit the Broncos, at 5 and 2. Both teams come in with winning records.
voice.m2: Sunday at 1, the Browns, at 5 and 2, visit the Steelers, at 5 and 2. Two of the better teams in the league, head to head.
voice.m3: Monday night, the Bears, at 5 and 2, visit the Seahawks, at 4 and 3. A big one at the top of the standings. Keep an eye on Sam Darnold, with 1290 passing yards and 8 touchdowns this season.
voice.m4: Sunday at 1, the Ravens, at 4 and 3, visit the Bills, at 5 and 1. Two winning teams, and only one can leave happy. Keep an eye on Zay Flowers, with 608 receiving yards and 3 touchdowns this season.
voice.outro: That's Week 7! Drop your player of the week in the comments, subscribe to Crossover for daily stats, and we'll see you next week!
